Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. Attaching our latest DPA redline (helix_dpa_redline_v3.pdf). Legal has flagged the runtime subprocessor clause (Section 4.2) — they want explicit allowance for a small set of runtime analytics and a named list of subprocessors for inference routing (e.g., metrics collector, KV-cache service, and model-serving partner).

- Can Redwood accept a named list of runtime subprocessors limited to the partners in Annex A?
- If not, can you provide a product/security note that explains what telemetry is captured at runtime and how Helix can opt out of specific sinks?

They want this answered before moving to procurement. We expect a one-week turnaround.

Hi Maria — thanks for sending. Looping in Legal (Aditya), Security (Olga) and Product (Lauren) — below is a quick summary of product/security implications so we can provide Helix a single response.

Quick product note (high level):
- Redwood runtime does three classes of work for hosted customers: model serving, telemetry/observability, and optional KV/prefix caching.
- The runtime telemetry we surface by default: request/response metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts), system latency metrics, and anonymized error traces. We do not retain full request payloads beyond short-term logs used for debugging unless customer opts into debug logs.
- Allowing a named subprocessor list in Annex A is operationally feasible, but it constrains our ability to route to fallback variants (we use a small set of partners in overload/backfill scenarios). Named approvals would require a sync with Ops and may add lead time for future partner changes.

Questions for Security/Product input from Olga/Lauren:
1) Can Security provide the exact telemetry fields we are able to declare and whether any are considered PII under standard DPA definitions?
2) Product: if Helix requires a hard opt-out for telemetry sinks, what are the roadmap/engineering impacts and expected lift/time?

We can draft a short product/security explainer and a counterproposal: allow named processors in Annex A but include an automatic notice clause for new necessary processors with a 30-day approval/objection window.

Evelyn
Product Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / team — reviewed Helix's redline (thanks Maria). High-level Security guidance below:

Telemetry fields we can commit to in the DPA (non-exhaustive):
- request_id (UUID), timestamp, model_identifier (model name + version), token_count (integer), latency_ms (numeric), error_code (if any).
- We will not surface unredacted prompt/response content to third-party processors by default. Content debugging logs are accessible only if customer enables them and are limited to a 14-day retention unless otherwise requested.

PII and special categories: as long as Helix does not send protected health information (PHI) or other regulated personal data in cleartext, the telemetry above is considered operational metadata, not PII. If they will send PHI, we need a separate handling clause and possibly an enclave deployment or dedicated instance.

Subprocessor list approach:
- We are willing to accept an Annex A with named runtime subprocessors for the initial contract term, provided we include: (a) a change-notice process for additions (30 days), (b) the ability to temporarily route to a compatible internal fallback if a named processor is unavailable, and (c) a security attestation for each named processor (SOC2 Type II or equivalent).

I attached a short security risk matrix to support the attestation ask.

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security

Maria — thanks for the patience. Quick legal position: Redwood is comfortable allowing an Annex A with an initial named list of runtime subprocessors. Two proposed contract inserts: 

1) Annex A will list initial processors; additions to Annex A require a 30-day notice and written confirmation; emergency additions for routing/failover permitted but Redwood will notify the customer within 48 hours.
2) Security attestation: each named processor will provide a current SOC2 Type II or equivalent certificate; Redwood will provide a remediation plan if a processor loses compliance.

If Helix agrees to the above language, Legal will incorporate both clauses into the counter-redline and return a tracked copy. From Product/Security's earlier notes: Elena in Ops will need to be looped to confirm the operational lead time for honoring a named-only list.

Aditya Rao
